The architecture for a Stable Diffusion model is specified through a complex pipeline of neural networks, primarily centered around a **Latent Diffusion Model (LDM)**. It is not a single "structure" but a coordinated system of three main components:

1.  **The Variational Autoencoder (VAE):** This is the "compressor." It maps high-resolution images into a lower-dimensional "latent space." Instead of processing every pixel (which is computationally expensive), the model works on these compressed mathematical representations.
2.  **The U-Net:** This is the "engine" of the diffusion process. It is trained to predict and remove noise from the latent representation. It takes a noisy latent input and, guided by text, iteratively refines it until a coherent image structure emerges.
3.  **The Text Encoder (usually CLIP):** This is the "interpreter." It converts your natural language prompts into embeddings (vectors) that the U-Net can understand. It ensures that when you type "a golden cathedral," the U-Net knows which visual features to prioritize.

**In summary:** The architecture is specified as a **conditional diffusion process** where a U-Net operates on a latent space provided by a VAE, guided by embeddings from a CLIP text encoder.
